title: Why checking your investments makes you worse at investing
description:
The more often you look, the more losses you see, and the worse your decisions get.

New video every day.

scenes.say: Two people own the same fund. One checks it every day. One checks it once a year. After thirty years they do not have the same amount.
Markets rise over long stretches and fall over short ones. Check daily, and you will see a losing day about half the time.
Check once a year, and you mostly see a number that has gone up.
Same fund. Same returns. A completely different emotional experience.
And emotion is what moves your finger. The person watching every loss is the person who sells during the crash.
Looking at your money more often does not give you more control. It gives you more chances to panic.
